messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency breach detected on dedicated-pool-eu-west-2 (model: rwd-7b-quant) — p99 ~ 3.6s (SLO 1.5s). Queue depth spiked to 1.1k. Auto-scaler attempted scale but observed 90s cold start delay. Paging oncall.
ali_oncall: I’m on it. seeing streaming stalls on 3 nodes, lots of requests stuck in WAITING. grabbing recent logs.
maya_sre: pinging infra, I’m seeing autoscaler events: scale request at 3790000012, pods Pending until 3790000078. warmup agent reports 2m warmup for this model image on those instances.
devon_runtime: hmm our warmup hook for quantized models still does big KV init. adding metrics: kv_init_ms=118000, kernel_jit_ms=41000 on those hosts.
ali_oncall: customer impact? eric_support pls share any tickets.
eric_support: two enterprise customers reported streaming timeouts and partial outputs — support ticket IDs #5632, #5633. both on dedicated capacity. they see many aborted streams, some clients retrying and hitting throttles.
sylvia_prodeng: critical: this is causing p95 regression too — p95 850ms -> 1.9s in last 5m. we should consider temporary routing to hosted pool or a compatible smaller model to keep latency.
ops-bot: Degradation policy applied: route_fallback_policy(dedicated-pool-eu-west-2 -> hosted-eu) activated by maya_sre at 3790000120.
maya_sre: rolling routing applied. telemetry shows ~20% of requests now hitting hosted fallback. latency downstream improved but tail still high for streaming sessions.
ali_oncall: investigating queue backlog. current snapshot: total_inflight=420, queue_depth=980, avg_queue_wait=2800ms, stream_stalls=12/min.
devon_runtime: trying a manual scale: increasing pool capacity now (requested +6 GPUs). note: nodes come healthy in ~70-90s.
ali_oncall: started manual bump at 3790000205. also dropping conservative warmup timeout on pool registration to allow earlier handshake: warmup_deadline=45s for now (temp).
sylvia_prodeng: careful — dropping warmup_deadline might cause cold-path stalls if model isn't KV-ready; but we need mitigations to reduce customer timeouts.
maya_sre: meanwhile adding KV cache warm-priming for popular prefixes (best-effort). kicked off priming job against new nodes.
devon_runtime: logs from node gpux-12: \n```\n[3790000234] model_load: quant layers loaded\n[3790000250] kv_init: started\n[3790000300] kv_init: 1/4 shards primed\n[3790000350] model_ready: true\n```\npattern: kv_init is the blocker.
ali_oncall: ok, manual scale completed; new capacity marked ready at 3790000401. queue depth dropped to 220 within 30s. p99 down to 1.4s after routing + scale.
eric_support: customers updated. they saw partial recovery and some retries cleared. still monitoring.
sylvia_prodeng: action items: short-term: keep fallback route active for 30m, keep raised capacity until autoscaler policies tuned. medium-term: reduce KV init time or snapshot priming at image build. long-term: add predictive ramping for scheduled bursts.
maya_sre: creating an incident record and will escalate to eng-runtime for a hotfix. put paging on eng-runtime after 15m if metrics do not stabilize.
ali_oncall: handoff to night oncall in 20m — will document current state and actions in ops-runbook. hooking in devon for next steps on warmup optimizations.
devon_runtime: immediate patch ideas: parallel KV shard init, persist warmed snapshot, and reduce kernel_jit on first host. I’ll open a PR with a feature flag.
ops-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, impact=multiple enterprise customers, mitigation=hosted-fallback + manual scale + KV priming.
maya_sre: timeline note: root cause likely autoscaler-request-to-available startup latency combined with heavy KV init on quant models leading to queue amplification under burst.
ali_oncall: thanks team. will file a postmortem template, include timelines, customer impact, and next steps. folks please drop any logs/snippets here before handoff.
devon_runtime: dropping a sample diag command for postmortem: \n```\nkubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide --selector=pool=dedicated-eu\nkubectl logs -f gpux-12 -c runtime --since=5m\ncurl -sS http://telemetry.internal/pools/dedicated-eu/metrics | jq '.autoscaler, .queue_depth, .kv_init_ms'\n```\nali_oncall: handoff complete; leaving monitoring on. last check p99=1.2s, queue_depth=80. handing to night oncall @ 3790000900.
ops-bot: Incident channel pinned with runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-autoscale-kv-init
maya_sre: postmortem owner assigned: sylvia_prodeng. thanks everyone for quick mitigation.
